questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
options: My father work in a bank.
My father works in a bank.
My father working in a bank.
My father is work in a bank.
questions.explanation: In the present simple, the verb takes -s with he/she/it, so 'My father works'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'A bus is ______ than a bicycle.'
questions.explanation: Short adjectives add -er and use 'than' to compare two things: 'faster than'.

questions.prompt: Which word means 'the money a person receives from work'?
questions.explanation: 'Income' is the money a person earns or receives, usually from work.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'That is the market ______ we buy our vegetables.'
questions.explanation: Use 'where' to refer to a place: 'the market where we buy our vegetables'.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence to give advice.
questions.explanation: After the modal 'should', use the base verb with no 'to': 'You should rest'.

questions.prompt: What does 'deforestation' mean?
options: Cutting down large numbers of trees
Watering crops in a dry season
questions.explanation: 'Deforestation' is the cutting down of large numbers of trees in an area.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct sentence.
questions.explanation: Use 'has' + the past participle 'written' (write – wrote – written): 'He has written'.

questions.prompt: Change to the passive: 'Workers clean the streets every morning.'
options: The streets are cleaned every morning.
The streets is cleaned every morning.
The streets were cleaned every morning.
questions.explanation: Present passive uses am/is/are + past participle; 'streets' is plural, so 'are cleaned'.

questions.prompt: "The doorbell is ringing!" Which reply shows a decision made at that moment?
options: I am going to open it.
questions.explanation: A decision made at the moment of speaking uses 'will': 'I will open it'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'There isn't ______ furniture in the new office.'
questions.explanation: 'Furniture' is uncountable, so use 'much' in this negative sentence: 'much furniture'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'If the bus ______ late, we will miss the meeting.'
questions.explanation: The if-clause of the first conditional uses the present simple: 'If the bus is late'.

questions.prompt: Complete: 'Of all my subjects, English is the ______.'
questions.explanation: Long adjectives form the superlative with 'the most': 'the most interesting'.

questions.prompt: Read: 'She is a cautious driver who never takes risks on the road.' The word 'cautious' means...
questions.explanation: A 'cautious' person is careful and avoids danger, which matches 'never takes risks'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence means 'it is not necessary'?
options: You mustn't bring your own lunch.
You don't have to bring your own lunch.
You must bring your own lunch.
You can't bring your own lunch.
questions.explanation: 'Don't have to' means an action is not necessary; 'mustn't' would mean it is forbidden.

questions.prompt: Read: 'Although the new factory created many jobs, residents complained that it polluted the nearby river.' What does the passage suggest about the factory?
options: It brought both a benefit and a problem.
questions.explanation: The factory gave a benefit (jobs) but caused a problem (pollution), shown by 'Although'.

questions.prompt: Combine: 'I spoke to the nurse. Her advice saved my life.' Best combined sentence:
options: I spoke to the nurse who advice saved my life.
I spoke to the nurse whose advice saved my life.
I spoke to the nurse which advice saved my life.
I spoke to the nurse who's advice saved my life.
questions.explanation: 'Whose' shows possession (her advice), so 'the nurse whose advice saved my life'.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that describes an imaginary, unlikely situation.
options: If you boil water, it turns to steam.
If it snows tomorrow, school will close.
If I were the president, I would lower taxes.
If you press this button, the light turns on.
questions.explanation: The second conditional ('If I were... I would...') describes an imaginary, unlikely situation.

questions.prompt: Complete with the correct word form: 'The committee will ______ the new rules next week.'
questions.explanation: After 'will' the sentence needs the base verb 'enforce'; 'enforcement' is a noun.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct passive sentence for: 'Someone has stolen my bicycle.'
options: My bicycle is stolen by someone yesterday.
questions.explanation: The present perfect passive is 'has/have been + past participle': 'has been stolen'.

questions.prompt: Choose the grammatically correct sentence.
options: He gave us a useful information about the job.
He gave us a few useful information about the job.
He gave us some useful information about the job.
He gave us many useful informations about the job.
questions.explanation: 'Information' is uncountable, so use 'some' and no plural -s: 'some useful information'.

questions.prompt: Read: 'By the time the volunteers arrived, the floodwater had already destroyed most of the harvest.' What happened first?
options: Both happened at the same time.
questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had destroyed' shows the destruction happened before the volunteers arrived.

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence with correct and consistent tenses.
options: When she arrived home, she realised that she leaves her keys at work.
When she arrived home, she realised that she had left her keys at work.
When she arrives home, she realised she has left her keys at work.
When she arrived home, she realise that she left her keys at work.
questions.explanation: The earlier action uses the past perfect ('had left') with the later past action ('realised').

questions.prompt: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: 'The government launched a campaign to ______ awareness about clean water.'
questions.explanation: The fixed collocation is 'raise awareness'; 'raise' is the transitive verb meaning to increase.

questions.prompt: Read: 'Far from discouraging her, the early failures made her even more determined to succeed.' How did the failures affect her?
options: They had no effect on her.
questions.explanation: 'Far from discouraging her' means the opposite happened: the failures increased her determination.
